ludwig-crocius.name: Ludwig Crocius
ludwig-crocius.bio: Bremen Reformed pastor and professor at the Gymnasium Illustre. A Dort delegate for Bremen, he stood for Melanchthonian irenicism and moderate orthodoxy rather than high Calvinist strictness, and his Syntagma sacrae theologiae (1636) is the chief systematic statement of that Bremen school.

louis-le-blanc-de-beaulieu.name: Louis Le Blanc de Beaulieu
louis-le-blanc-de-beaulieu.bio: Reformed professor of theology at the Academy of Sedan. His Theological Theses map Protestant and Roman Catholic positions with unusual clarity and restraint; John Owen praised his moderation on justification. Distinctive for irenic comparison without surrendering Reformed confession.

john-davenant.name: John Davenant
john-davenant.bio: Lady Margaret Professor at Cambridge, later Bishop of Salisbury, and a British delegate at the Synod of Dort. He defended Reformed predestination while arguing a broad sufficiency of Christ's death for all—an English moderate-orthodox line often linked with later hypothetical universalism.

robert-baron.name: Robert Baron
robert-baron.bio: Reformed philosophy professor at St Salvator's College, St Andrews. Philosophia theologiae ancillans treats philosophy as the handmaid of theology: scholastic metaphysics ordered to Reformed doctrinal ends, not free-standing speculation.

josue-de-la-place.name: Josué de la Place (Placeus)
josue-de-la-place.bio: Reformed professor at the Academy of Saumur. Best known for denying the immediate imputation of Adam's first sin, teaching mediate imputation instead—a signature Saumur position contested by stricter Reformed orthodoxy and later condemned in some synodical debates.

epiphanius-of-salamis.name: Epiphanius of Salamis
epiphanius-of-salamis.bio: Bishop of Salamis (Constantia) on Cyprus. Best known for the Panarion (Medicine Chest), a vast catalogue of heresies, with the Ancoratus as a shorter doctrinal anchor for the churches. A fierce defender of Nicene orthodoxy and monastic discipline.

nemesius-of-emesa.name: Nemesius of Emesa
nemesius-of-emesa.bio: Bishop of Emesa (Homs) writing near the end of the fourth century. On the Nature of Man joins Christian doctrine to Greek philosophical psychology—soul, body, providence, and free will—in a synthesis widely read in East and West.

julius-africanus.name: Julius Africanus
julius-africanus.bio: Sextus Julius Africanus, Christian chronographer and encyclopedist of the early third century. His Chronographiai ordered world history to the Incarnation; the Cesti (Embroidered Girdles) is a learned miscellany of military, medical, and technical lore of which only fragments survive.

serapion-of-antioch.name: Serapion of Antioch
serapion-of-antioch.bio: Bishop of Antioch around the turn of the third century. Surviving fragments show a churchman guarding apostolic teaching, including caution about which gospels the churches should read.

samuel-strimesius.name: Samuel Strimesius
samuel-strimesius.bio: Reformed doctor of theology and primary preacher in the church and university at Frankfurt an der Oder (Viadrina). He labored for ecclesiastical peace among Evangelicals, weighing Lutheran–Reformed controversies by Scripture, and wrote irenic Latin works including Ingenua in Controversias Evangelicorum (1708) and Ingenua in Arminianismum Inquisitio (1703). Distinctive as a Frankfurt (Oder) faculty voice that distinguishes fundamental consensus from less-than-fundamental dissent rather than recycling only the stricter Genevan or Puritan lines.
